To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cryptic recombination signal (cRS) elements are conserved at the 5′ ends of Vκ gene segments in mice and that they are cleaved in the pre-B cell line, 103/BCL-2, and in mouse bone marrow B cell populations.

cryptic recombination sites in Vκ gene sequences are conserved and are cleaved at an early stage of B cell differentiation, and that the pattern of their conservation is similar to the pattern of conservation of cryptic recombination sequences in VH gene sequences.
we have discovered conserved cryptic RS in Vκ gene segment, which we have shown are cleaved in B cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the generation of the immunoglobulin repertoire and the mechanisms of B cell development.
the mechanisms that regulate antibody diversity, and the role that this diversity plays in maintaining the health of the immune system.
the molecular mechanism of the generation of the immunoglobulin genes expressed by B cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cRS are present in Vκ gene segment but that their presence is not due to selection pressure to maintain cRS to mediate VH replacement.
cRS are cleaved in B cells and are conserved in Vκ and VH gene segments.
the cRS are not conserved to facilitate receptor editing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
V(D)J cleavage occurs at cRS in small B lymphoid cells, that these cells are not yet able to recognize exogenous antigen, and that the cleavage of cRS is a conserved process.
cRS cleavage occurs in pre-B cells and is not dependent on antigenic stimulation, but is dependent on the 12/12 and 23/23 rule.
the cleavage of cryptic recombination signal sequences is an evolutionarily conserved feature of the V(D)J recombinase system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cleavage of Vκ cRS is a general property of pre-B cells, which may have implications for the development of BCRs with autoreactivity.
the V(D)J recombinase is active in pre-B cells, and this activity is independent of B cell antigen receptor (BCR) specificity.
cRS are cleaved in B cells that cannot interact with exogenous antigen.
